# XDR105: Must<Arm>() on a multi-arm union without a dominating discriminant check

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | XDR1xx: trusting unvalidated fields |
| How to fix | switch on the union's type, or use the ok result of Get<Arm>(), before calling Must<Arm>() |
| Default severity | warning (`severity: {XDR105: …}` changes it) |
| Default rule set | no: opt-in, add XDR105 to `rules` |
| Guide | [Validated versus unvalidated fields](../../guide/indexer-hardening.mdx#validated-fields) |
| Self-audit checklist item | HC-107 |
| Demonstrating corpus entry | `cap-0067/token-events-bytes-and-bad-type-muxed-id` (registered in [corpus/plan.json](../../corpus/plan.json)) |
| Fixtures | [lint/testdata/xdr1xx/xdr105](../testdata/xdr1xx/xdr105) |

## What it reports

`Must<Arm>()` on a union with more than one arm, at a point not dominated by a check of the same value's
discriminant (a `switch` on its type, a comparison, or the `ok` result of the matching `Get<Arm>()`).

## Why it matters

The `Must…` accessors panic when the value holds another arm. Which arm a field of a ledger holds is chosen by the
submitter or a contract wherever the protocol allows several, so an unchecked `Must…` lets a ledger crash the
reader.

## Example

Reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr1xx/xdr105/bad.go
func memoText(m xdr.Memo) string {
	return m.MustText()
}
```

Not reported:

```go
// lint/testdata/xdr1xx/xdr105/good.go
func memoTextChecked(m xdr.Memo) string {
	if m.Type != xdr.MemoTypeMemoText {
		return ""
	}
	return m.MustText()
}
```

## Limits

Opt-in, because the rule cannot know protocol facts that fix the arm (for example that a successful operation of
one type always has a result of the matching arm) and reports such calls too.

## Configure and suppress

Turn the rule off by leaving XDR105 out of `rules` in `.xdrlint.yml` or a profile. To accept one report, put `//xdrlint:ignore XDR105 <reason>` on the reported line or on the enclosing function's doc comment (under golangci-lint, `//nolint:xdrlint // <reason>`), or add an entry to an external suppression file for code you cannot edit. A suppression needs a reason, and one that suppresses nothing is itself reported (XDR000). See [Configuring and suppressing](README.md#linter-suppressions).
